name: Chromatophore Nail Modification
description: Introduces chromatophore cells into the nail beds of fingers and toes, allowing voluntary color-shifting of the nails across the full visible spectrum. The nails can display solid colors, gradients, patterns, and even simple animated effects. Combined with structural coloration from morpho butterfly genes, the nails produce iridescent, holographic-quality color effects that no nail polish can replicate. The modification has completely replaced the nail polish industry in Meridian 88. Nail salons now offer chromatophore pattern programming rather than paint application. Animated nail displays synchronized with music or conversation are considered high art. The modification is inexpensive, painless, and nearly universal — it's difficult to find someone in Meridian 88 under age 50 with unmodified nails.
source_organism: Sepia officinalis (common cuttlefish), Morpho menelaus (blue morpho butterfly, structural coloration)
manufacturer: Widespread — available at every gene clinic and many pharmacies
procedure: Nail bed injection, self-administered or clinic-applied, single session
side_effects: Nails become slightly softer than unmodified keratin
Color shifts may lag by a second during rapid changes
Rare: chromatophore migration to cuticle skin causing colored patches around nails
social_perception: Universal. Chromatic nails are the most common geneware modification in existence. They're so common that unmodified nails are remarkable. The modification is considered baseline personal grooming.
story_hooks: A nail chromatophore pattern is used as a visual passcode for a secret organization — members identify each other by displaying a specific animated sequence that only members know
A pharmacy's nail modification kit is contaminated with a gene tracker that reports the user's location through the chromatophore cells' electrical activity
